text: Two athletes have the same BMI, but one has substantially greater lean mass. Which limitation of BMI explains why their performance profiles may differ?
options: It does not separate fat mass from lean mass
It directly measures regional fat distribution
It includes a valid estimate of muscle quality
explanation: BMI uses body mass and height but cannot distinguish adipose tissue from muscle, bone or other fat-free mass.

text: During repeated football sprints, which adaptation most directly supports recovery between high-intensity efforts late in a match?
explanation: Aerobic oxidative metabolism supports phosphocreatine resynthesis and helps process metabolites during the recovery periods between sprints.

text: An athlete feels repeated ankle giving-way despite negative stress radiographs after a healed sprain. Which impairment most likely explains the functional instability?
explanation: Functional instability can persist because sensorimotor and neuromuscular deficits remain even when mechanical laxity is not demonstrated.

text: A sprinter reduces the posteriorly directed horizontal ground-reaction impulse during early stance. What is the most direct performance consequence?
options: A larger vertical oscillation of the centre of mass
A longer braking phase during contact
A greater dependence on passive knee stability
Less horizontal deceleration of forward velocity
explanation: The braking impulse opposes forward motion. Reducing it limits horizontal deceleration and helps preserve forward velocity.

text: Why should an isolated post-match creatine-kinase value not be used as a stand-alone decision to reduce an athlete's training?
options: No effect from eccentric or contact work
explanation: Creatine kinase can show a delayed, highly variable response influenced by exercise mode, muscle damage and individual biology; it should be interpreted with other information.

text: Which approach best represents progressive overload in an elite training programme?
options: Increase external load every session regardless of fatigue
Adjust load, volume and intensity while monitoring response
Change exercises frequently without tracking performance
Increase training frequency while removing recovery days
explanation: Progressive overload is planned relative to the athlete's response; manipulating load and volume while monitoring fatigue is safer than applying a fixed increase.

text: Which construct most directly describes an athlete's ability to maintain effective attention and confidence under competitive pressure?
explanation: Mental toughness is commonly described through resilience, attentional control, confidence and effective emotional regulation under pressure.

text: Why is adequate carbohydrate availability especially important during repeated high-intensity training?
options: Removes the need for fluid replacement
Provides more energy than fat at rest
explanation: Glycogenolysis and glycolysis can supply ATP rapidly enough for high-intensity work, whereas fat oxidation cannot match that rate.

text: In the Heath-Carter notation 1-7-1, which component is most prominent?
explanation: The middle number represents mesomorphy, so 1-7-1 indicates a very strong mesomorphic component with low endomorphy and ectomorphy.

text: A late-maturing junior athlete has good technical skill but is temporarily smaller than peers. What is the most defensible performance-support recommendation?
explanation: Current size can disadvantage later maturers in selection, but longitudinal monitoring avoids confusing temporary maturation status with long-term potential.

text: A countermovement-jump test gives very similar results when the same athlete repeats it under the same conditions. Which property is demonstrated?
explanation: Reliability concerns consistency or reproducibility of measurements, whereas validity concerns whether the test measures the intended construct.

text: A field test is considered valid for a performance decision when it primarily:
explanation: Validity is the extent to which a test measures or supports the intended inference, not simply how precise, long or expensive the procedure is.

text: Before a force-plate testing session, which action most directly improves the comparability of measurements?
options: Use a different warm-up each time
explanation: Calibration, zeroing and a documented standard procedure reduce avoidable measurement error and support comparison across trials.

text: Before a maximal exercise test, the athlete should first receive relevant information about the procedure and voluntarily agree to participate. This is:
explanation: Informed consent requires understandable information, an opportunity to ask questions and a voluntary decision before participation.

text: Three sprint times are 10, 12 and 14 seconds. What is their arithmetic mean?
explanation: The arithmetic mean is (10 + 12 + 14) / 3 = 12 seconds.

text: A team finds that weekly training load and injury reports rise together. What conclusion is justified from this correlation alone?
options: Load reduction removes all injury risk
explanation: Correlation describes an association; confounding, reverse causation and measurement issues must be considered before making a causal inference.

text: A training intervention produces p < 0.05 but only a trivial change in sprint time. Which additional statistic is most useful for judging practical importance?
explanation: Effect size estimates the magnitude of change, and its confidence interval helps communicate precision and practical uncertainty beyond statistical significance.

text: To interpret a six-week trend in repeated jump testing, the analyst should first:
explanation: Consistent protocols and conditions make longitudinal changes more interpretable and help distinguish real change from measurement noise.

text: Repeated sets show a velocity loss well above the athlete's prescribed threshold. What is the most appropriate immediate adjustment?
explanation: Excessive velocity loss suggests the planned dose is exceeding the current response; the session should be adjusted rather than escalated without assessment.

text: An athlete reports repeated short sleep and worsening reaction time during a congested competition week. Which first-line strategy is most defensible?
explanation: Adequate sleep opportunity and practical sleep-hygiene adjustments are foundational recovery measures; stimulants do not replace sleep.

text: Which description best fits low-intensity active recovery after a demanding session?
explanation: Active recovery uses low-intensity movement that is unlikely to create a meaningful additional training load while supporting comfortable movement and circulation.

text: Which change is commonly associated with successful heat acclimatization?
options: Lower plasma volume and earlier drift
Expanded plasma volume and better sweating
Less need for fluids and sodium
explanation: Heat acclimatization can expand plasma volume and improve sweating and cardiovascular responses, although it does not remove environmental risk.

text: For an eastward journey across several time zones, which planning principle usually helps the athlete adapt?
explanation: Eastward travel generally requires phase advance. Sleep timing and appropriately timed light exposure should be planned, while alcohol is not a sound treatment.

text: Performance is falling while perceived fatigue and soreness remain high across several sessions. Which programme response is most defensible?
explanation: A temporary reduction in training stress allows recovery and helps determine whether the decline reflects excessive load, illness, injury or another factor.

text: A team uses GPS-derived high-speed running distance to guide training. What is the essential first safeguard?
options: Treat a high value as injury
explanation: GPS measures can vary with device, sampling rate, movement and environment; their measurement properties and practical context should be understood before decisions are made.

text: An inertial measurement unit used in sport commonly combines sensors that estimate:
explanation: IMUs commonly contain accelerometers and gyroscopes, with some systems also using magnetometers, to characterize movement.

text: A statistically significant difference is found between two training groups. Which statement remains necessary?
options: Superiority is proven for every athlete
Significance is unaffected by sample size
explanation: Statistical significance does not establish practical importance or universal superiority; effect size, confidence intervals and context are also relevant.

subtopic: Athlete data governance and AI ethics
text: An athlete-management system uses an algorithm to flag injury risk. Which practice best supports responsible use?
explanation: Responsible athlete-data use requires purpose limitation, appropriate access and protection, transparency about uncertainty, and human clinical oversight.

text: A previously motivated athlete reports emotional exhaustion and detachment from sport. Which support response is most appropriate?
explanation: Burnout risk should prompt a supportive, multidisciplinary review of stress, recovery, motivation and athlete autonomy rather than blame or coercion.

text: When pranayama is introduced into an athlete's programme, which principle is most appropriate?
options: Forceful breath holds for all athletes
explanation: Breathing practices should be taught progressively and safely; they may complement but do not replace appropriate training or clinical assessment.

text: What is the main value of a shared athlete-management record within a multidisciplinary team?
explanation: A well-governed shared record supports continuity and coordinated decisions while still requiring role-based access and professional judgement.

text: A coach asks for an athlete's private clinical details in a group chat. What should the physiotherapist do first?
options: Share the complete record with the team
Obtain consent and share necessary details
explanation: Confidential clinical information should be shared on a need-to-know basis through appropriate channels, with the athlete's informed consent except where a lawful exception applies.

text: The first modern Olympic Games of the Olympiad were held in which city in 1896?
explanation: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece, in 1896.

text: The inaugural Asian Games were held in 1951 in which city?
explanation: The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi in 1951.

text: Which description best matches the broad purpose of the Khelo India scheme?
options: A replacement for all National Federations
explanation: Khelo India is a national programme with components for participation, competitions, talent identification, development and sports infrastructure.

text: Within TOPS, the Mission Olympic Cell is most closely associated with:
explanation: The Mission Olympic Cell is the decision-making and review mechanism associated with TOPS support for identified elite athletes and proposals.

text: A TUE is intended to allow an athlete to:
options: Use a justified TUE under the criteria
Declare a supplement safe without checks
Transfer medication decisions to a coach
explanation: A Therapeutic Use Exemption permits specified use of a prohibited substance or method when the international standard's criteria are met and the process is followed.

text: The Athlete Biological Passport primarily monitors:
explanation: The ABP uses longitudinal biological data to identify atypical patterns that may warrant further anti-doping action.

text: The 2026 FIFA World Cup is being hosted across which countries?
explanation: The 2026 FIFA World Cup is a joint tournament hosted by Canada, Mexico and the United States.

text: When an athlete reports possible harassment within a sports programme, the most appropriate first organisational response is to:
options: Ask for private resolution with the accused
explanation: Safeguarding systems should provide a safe reporting route, protect the person from retaliation and preserve confidentiality while the matter is handled through the proper process.

text: Weakness of the serratus anterior with medial scapular winging most strongly suggests involvement of which nerve?
explanation: The long thoracic nerve supplies serratus anterior; weakness can impair scapular protraction and upward rotation and produce medial winging.

text: Which nerve supplies the gluteus medius?
explanation: The superior gluteal nerve supplies gluteus medius, gluteus minimus and tensor fasciae latae.

text: The primary mechanical role of the anterior cruciate ligament is to resist excessive:
explanation: The ACL is a major restraint to anterior tibial translation and also contributes to rotational stability of the knee.

text: Numbness in the thumb, index, middle and radial half of the ring finger with symptoms provoked at the carpal tunnel most implicates the:
explanation: The median nerve passes through the carpal tunnel and supplies sensation to the described palmar digits.

text: Cardiac output during exercise is calculated as:
options: Heart rate multiplied by stroke volume
Stroke volume divided by heart rate
Systolic pressure multiplied by respiratory rate
Venous return divided by oxygen extraction
explanation: Cardiac output is the volume pumped per minute and equals heart rate multiplied by stroke volume.

text: Compared with type IIx fibres, type I fibres are generally characterised by:
explanation: Type I fibres have relatively high oxidative capacity and are more resistant to fatigue, although fibre properties exist on a continuum.

text: During an incremental test, ventilation begins to rise disproportionately to oxygen uptake as metabolic acidosis increases. This point is most consistent with:
explanation: The ventilatory threshold is identified by a disproportionate increase in ventilation relative to oxygen uptake and is related to increasing acid-base buffering demands.

text: Which adaptation is expected after appropriate heat acclimatization?
options: Lower plasma volume after heat training
Better sweating and circulation in heat
explanation: Heat acclimatization improves thermoregulatory and cardiovascular responses, commonly including earlier sweating and plasma-volume expansion.

text: During acclimatization to sustained altitude exposure, increased erythropoietin primarily promotes:
explanation: Reduced oxygen availability stimulates erythropoietin, which supports increased red-cell production over time; it does not restore ambient oxygen pressure.

text: The immediate analgesic effect of conventional high-frequency TENS is most closely associated with:
explanation: Conventional TENS is commonly explained through activation of non-nociceptive afferents and modulation of nociceptive transmission at spinal levels.

text: When the target tissue is relatively superficial, which therapeutic-ultrasound frequency is generally selected?
explanation: Within conventional therapeutic ultrasound practice, 3 MHz is absorbed more superficially than 1 MHz and is therefore selected for shallower targets.

text: Which history requires particular caution and device-specific review before applying electrical stimulation?
explanation: Implanted electronic devices require careful review because electrical stimulation may interfere with device function depending on the modality and application.

text: Compared with continuous ultrasound, pulsed ultrasound is selected when the clinician wants to:
options: Deliver no acoustic energy at all
explanation: Pulsing lowers the temporal average intensity and can reduce thermal accumulation compared with continuous delivery at the same peak settings.

text: A rehabilitation programme is progressed most appropriately when the athlete can complete the current dose with acceptable symptoms and control. This reflects:
explanation: Progression applies a gradually increasing challenge once the current workload is tolerated, while respecting symptoms, movement quality and the rehabilitation goal.

text: During a controlled lowering phase of a squat, the quadriceps are primarily performing which type of contraction?
explanation: The quadriceps develop tension while lengthening to control knee flexion during the lowering phase, which is an eccentric action.

text: In a hold-relax PNF technique, the target muscle is commonly followed by:
explanation: Hold-relax uses an isometric contraction of the target muscle followed by relaxation and a controlled attempt to access additional range.

subtopic: Open and closed kinetic chain exercise
text: Which exercise is a typical closed-kinetic-chain task for the lower limb?
explanation: In a closed kinetic chain, the distal segment is relatively fixed; a squat is performed with the feet in contact with the ground.

text: For a tolerable chronic tendon-loading programme, heavy slow resistance is primarily intended to:
options: Test the tendon at maximal speed
explanation: Heavy slow resistance uses progressively dosed, controlled loading to develop capacity while monitoring symptoms and function.

text: Maitland grade I mobilisation is best described as:
explanation: Grade I is a small-amplitude oscillation at the beginning of range, commonly used for pain modulation; larger or end-range grades differ in purpose.

text: Joint torque is most directly determined by the combination of:
options: Force magnitude and perpendicular moment arm
explanation: External or internal torque depends on force and its perpendicular distance from the axis of rotation.

text: Which feature is characteristic of loading response during normal walking?
options: Terminal swing with no ground contact
The opposite limb never contacts ground
explanation: Loading response follows initial contact and includes weight acceptance, controlled knee flexion and shock attenuation.

text: The commonly taught overall scapulohumeral contribution during full shoulder elevation is approximately:
explanation: The traditional teaching model describes roughly two degrees of glenohumeral movement for each degree of scapular upward rotation, while actual motion varies with task and phase.

text: The impulse delivered by a force is represented by the:
options: Peak velocity divided by contact time
Average force multiplied by body mass
Joint angle multiplied by angular speed
explanation: Impulse is the integral of force over time and equals the change in momentum.

text: An athlete improves maximal squat strength but not jump height. Which additional quality should be examined most directly?
explanation: Jumping requires force to be developed rapidly; maximal force can rise without a corresponding improvement in rate of force development.

text: A runner increases cadence modestly while maintaining speed and shows reduced peak knee loading. What is the most reasonable interpretation?
options: May reduce overstriding and knee load
explanation: A modest cadence increase can reduce step length and overstriding in some runners, potentially altering lower-limb loading; the response should be checked individually.

text: An athlete performs well in training but repeatedly struggles in competition. Which intervention most directly rehearses the performance context?
explanation: Graded pressure simulations can help the athlete practise attentional and coping skills in conditions that resemble competition.

text: An athlete continues a difficult drill because the challenge itself is enjoyable. This is most consistent with:
explanation: Intrinsic motivation involves engaging in an activity for interest, enjoyment, challenge or inherent satisfaction.

text: A young athlete reports exhaustion, reduced enjoyment and feeling controlled by adults. Which response is most appropriate?
options: Review stress and recovery; restore autonomy
explanation: Burnout prevention includes attention to recovery and an autonomy-supportive environment, with referral when symptoms require specialised care.

text: Which clinical test is generally regarded as the more sensitive bedside test for an ACL tear?
explanation: The Lachman test is commonly regarded as more sensitive for ACL insufficiency, while the pivot shift is often more specific for rotational instability.

text: Pain reproduced by the Hawkins-Kennedy manoeuvre most directly raises suspicion of irritation in the:
explanation: The Hawkins-Kennedy position can provoke subacromial pain involving structures such as the rotator-cuff tendons or bursa; it is not a stand-alone diagnosis.

text: A palpable defect and absent plantarflexion response during calf compression are most concerning for:
explanation: The Thompson or Simmonds calf-squeeze test assesses continuity of the gastrocnemius-soleus-Achilles mechanism; an absent response with a gap suggests rupture.

text: The FABER position places the tested hip into:
explanation: FABER stands for flexion, abduction and external rotation; the test may stress the hip and surrounding lumbopelvic structures.

text: The VISA-P questionnaire is designed primarily to monitor disability and symptoms related to:
explanation: VISA-P is a patient-reported measure developed for patellar tendinopathy symptoms and functional limitations.

text: In the PEACE and LOVE framework, the loading principle is intended to:
options: Protect the injury from all movement
Use passive modalities for a month
explanation: Optimal loading introduces graded movement and mechanical stress at a level appropriate to tissue irritability and healing stage.

text: Which finding after a head impact should prompt urgent medical assessment rather than continued sideline observation alone?
explanation: Repeated vomiting and deterioration in consciousness are red flags requiring urgent evaluation for potentially serious intracranial or cervical injury.

text: An athlete collapses in heat with central nervous system dysfunction and suspected exertional heat stroke. The priority is to:
options: Return to running after oral fluids
explanation: Exertional heat stroke is time-critical. Immediate whole-body cooling, commonly cold-water immersion where feasible, should begin while emergency support is activated.

text: For a team crossing multiple time zones, the most useful travel plan is to:
options: Plan sleep, light and destination training
explanation: Travel planning should be individualised where necessary and coordinate sleep, light, meals, exercise and recovery with the direction and duration of travel.

text: A female endurance athlete has persistent fatigue, recurrent illness and menstrual disturbance in the context of low energy availability. Which condition should be considered?
explanation: Low energy availability with health and performance consequences is consistent with the REDs clinical framework and warrants multidisciplinary assessment.

text: What is the safest general advice when an athlete asks about a commercial supplement with an unverified ingredient list?
options: Use it because supplements are not tested
Double the dose to test it
explanation: Supplements can be contaminated or inaccurately labelled. Evidence, need, product quality and anti-doping risk should be reviewed with appropriate professionals.

text: A study reports a mean treatment effect with a wide confidence interval. The most appropriate interpretation is that:
explanation: A wide confidence interval indicates imprecision around the estimate; the result may still inform decisions but should not be treated as highly certain.

subtopic: Doha taxonomy and adductor-related groin pain
text: A 23-year-old football midfielder has gradual groin pain after a rapid increase in small-sided games. Palpation is painful at the adductor longus origin, and resisted adduction reproduces the familiar pain. Which Doha category best fits?
explanation: Adductor tenderness together with pain reproduced by resisted adduction supports the adductor-related category in the Doha taxonomy.
passage: A 23-year-old football midfielder has gradual groin pain after a rapid increase in small-sided games. Palpation is painful at the adductor longus origin, and resisted adduction reproduces the familiar pain. Hip range is full and there is no palpable inguinal hernia.

text: Which additional finding would most strongly reinforce the working classification in this case?
explanation: The Doha approach links adductor-related groin pain to adductor tenderness and pain on resisted adduction or adductor testing.
passage: A 23-year-old football midfielder has gradual groin pain after a rapid increase in small-sided games. Palpation is painful at the adductor longus origin, and resisted adduction reproduces the familiar pain. Hip range is full and there is no palpable inguinal hernia.

text: Once irritability is controlled, which rehabilitation direction best addresses the athlete's likely limiting capacity?
explanation: Recovery requires progressive restoration of adductor capacity and exposure to the demands that provoked symptoms, rather than prolonged avoidance or an abrupt return.
passage: A 23-year-old football midfielder has gradual groin pain after a rapid increase in small-sided games. Palpation is painful at the adductor longus origin, and resisted adduction reproduces the familiar pain. Hip range is full and there is no palpable inguinal hernia.

text: Which new finding would make the clinician reconsider an isolated adductor-related classification and broaden the assessment?
options: Mild discomfort after a controlled strengthening set
Improved adductor strength over two weeks
Pain that is less intense during walking
Cough-related inguinal pain with focal canal tenderness
explanation: Cough-related inguinal pain and canal tenderness point toward an inguinal-related presentation and justify a broader differential assessment.
passage: A 23-year-old football midfielder has gradual groin pain after a rapid increase in small-sided games. Palpation is painful at the adductor longus origin, and resisted adduction reproduces the familiar pain. Hip range is full and there is no palpable inguinal hernia.

text: A 25-year-old fast bowler has dominant-shoulder external rotation gain and a 25-degree loss of internal rotation, with pain in late cocking. Which pattern is most consistent?
explanation: A relative loss of internal rotation with an external-rotation gain in an overhead athlete is a classic GIRD pattern, although the total arc and clinical context should also be assessed.
passage: A 25-year-old fast bowler has dominant-shoulder external rotation gain and a 25-degree loss of internal rotation, with pain in late cocking. Posterior shoulder tightness is present, but there is no traumatic dislocation.

text: Which early rehabilitation emphasis is most directly matched to the examination findings?
options: Immobilisation in a sling for six weeks
explanation: The findings support addressing posterior shoulder mobility and the strength and control demands of the scapula and rotator cuff while managing throwing load.
passage: A 25-year-old fast bowler has dominant-shoulder external rotation gain and a 25-degree loss of internal rotation, with pain in late cocking. Posterior shoulder tightness is present, but there is no traumatic dislocation.

text: Why is the late-cocking phase clinically important in this athlete?
options: It places no demand on the glenohumeral joint
It is defined by elbow extension without shoulder rotation
High external rotation and abduction before acceleration
It occurs only after the ball has left the hand
explanation: Late cocking places high external-rotation and abduction demands on the shoulder before the rapid acceleration phase, so mobility and control deficits can become consequential.
passage: A 25-year-old fast bowler has dominant-shoulder external rotation gain and a 25-degree loss of internal rotation, with pain in late cocking. Posterior shoulder tightness is present, but there is no traumatic dislocation.

text: If the clinician wants to examine supraspinatus force production while reducing the painful thumb-down position, which option is most appropriate?
explanation: A full-can or resisted scaption position is commonly used to examine supraspinatus function while avoiding some of the provocative internal-rotation position of an empty-can test.
passage: A 25-year-old fast bowler has dominant-shoulder external rotation gain and a 25-degree loss of internal rotation, with pain in late cocking. Posterior shoulder tightness is present, but there is no traumatic dislocation.

text: A 19-year-old fast bowler develops focal low-back pain that increases with repeated lumbar extension and ipsilateral rotation. There is no leg numbness. Which diagnosis should be prioritised?
explanation: Repetitive extension and rotation in young athletes, particularly fast bowlers, raises concern for a pars interarticularis stress injury.
passage: A 19-year-old fast bowler develops focal low-back pain that increases with repeated lumbar extension and ipsilateral rotation. There is no leg numbness. Neurological screening is normal, but the pain persists after a reduction in bowling volume.

text: Which new finding would most strongly shift the differential toward lumbar nerve-root involvement rather than an isolated pars stress injury?
options: Dermatomal leg pain with positive SLR
explanation: Dermatomal radiating pain and a positive neurodynamic test suggest nerve-root mechanosensitivity or radiculopathy and require a different clinical reasoning pathway.
passage: A 19-year-old fast bowler develops focal low-back pain that increases with repeated lumbar extension and ipsilateral rotation. There is no leg numbness. Neurological screening is normal, but the pain persists after a reduction in bowling volume.

text: If pain is localised near the posterior superior iliac spine, which approach is more defensible than relying on a single sacroiliac provocation test?
explanation: Sacroiliac pain assessment is more defensible when a cluster of concordant provocation tests is interpreted alongside history and other examination findings.
passage: A 19-year-old fast bowler develops focal low-back pain that increases with repeated lumbar extension and ipsilateral rotation. There is no leg numbness. Neurological screening is normal, but the pain persists after a reduction in bowling volume.

text: Because focal pain persists despite load reduction and the athlete is skeletally immature, the next step should be to:
options: Return to full bowling if strong
Medical review and imaging for bony stress
explanation: Persistent focal pain with a stress-injury pattern warrants medical review and appropriate imaging decisions; a normal neurological screen does not exclude a pars injury.
passage: A 19-year-old fast bowler develops focal low-back pain that increases with repeated lumbar extension and ipsilateral rotation. There is no leg numbness. Neurological screening is normal, but the pain persists after a reduction in bowling volume.

text: A rugby player is struck in the head, vomits twice and becomes increasingly drowsy. What is the most appropriate immediate decision?
options: Brief screen then return to play
explanation: Repeated vomiting and deterioration in conscious state are red flags in the SCAT6 framework and require urgent medical assessment rather than a routine sideline clearance.
passage: A rugby player is struck in the head during a tackle. He is briefly confused, vomits twice over the next ten minutes and becomes increasingly drowsy. The team medical area is beside the field and emergency services are available.

text: If the athlete's symptoms later settle while awaiting transfer, which return-to-play decision is appropriate that day?
options: Return after a normal balance test
No same-day return after suspected concussion
Return if the coach accepts the risk
Return after ten minutes of jogging
explanation: An athlete with suspected concussion should be removed from play and not return to sport on the same day; urgent assessment takes priority.
passage: A rugby player is struck in the head during a tackle. He is briefly confused, vomits twice over the next ten minutes and becomes increasingly drowsy. The team medical area is beside the field and emergency services are available.

text: For a stable athlete with no emergency red flags during later clinical assessment, SCAT6 is best understood as:
explanation: SCAT6 combines symptom, cognitive, neurological and balance elements but is one component of a broader clinical assessment and does not by itself provide clearance.
passage: A rugby player is struck in the head during a tackle. He is briefly confused, vomits twice over the next ten minutes and becomes increasingly drowsy. The team medical area is beside the field and emergency services are available.

subtopic: Graduated return to sport after concussion
text: When a medically supervised graduated return-to-sport programme is later started, which progression principle is most appropriate?
options: Advance through all stages in one session
Use symptoms only after full-contact practice
Increase intensity even when symptoms recur
explanation: Graduated return uses stepwise increases in activity, generally with at least 24 hours between stages and a return to the previous tolerated level if symptoms worsen.
passage: A rugby player is struck in the head during a tackle. He is briefly confused, vomits twice over the next ten minutes and becomes increasingly drowsy. The team medical area is beside the field and emergency services are available.

text: A footballer is 18 weeks after ACL reconstruction and asks for clearance because the calendar milestone has been reached. Which principle should guide the decision?
options: Clear when the scar is healed
Normal resting heart rate is sufficient
explanation: Return-to-sport decisions should integrate symptoms, impairments, functional performance, psychological readiness, sport demands and risk rather than relying on time alone.
passage: A 24-year-old footballer is 18 weeks after ACL reconstruction. He has no effusion at rest but shows 86% quadriceps limb symmetry on dynamometry, 88% on the crossover hop, and low confidence during unanticipated cutting. He wants clearance because the calendar milestone has been reached.

text: Which training modification best reflects the IOC load-management principle while this athlete is rebuilding football exposure?
options: Increase running, cutting and match minutes simultaneously
Progress load gradually and monitor response
Avoid all field exposure until a fixed one-year date
Use a single maximal session to test readiness
explanation: Load should be progressed in a planned manner with monitoring of response, recovery and injury risk rather than changed abruptly or avoided indefinitely.
passage: A 24-year-old footballer is 18 weeks after ACL reconstruction. He has no effusion at rest but shows 86% quadriceps limb symmetry on dynamometry, 88% on the crossover hop, and low confidence during unanticipated cutting. He wants clearance because the calendar milestone has been reached.

text: Which finding most clearly argues against immediate unrestricted football clearance in this case?
options: No effusion at rest after testing
Sub-90% function with poor cutting confidence
explanation: The combined functional and psychological deficits indicate that the athlete has not met the programme's readiness criteria for unrestricted high-demand sport.
passage: A 24-year-old footballer is 18 weeks after ACL reconstruction. He has no effusion at rest but shows 86% quadriceps limb symmetry on dynamometry, 88% on the crossover hop, and low confidence during unanticipated cutting. He wants clearance because the calendar milestone has been reached.

text: What is the most appropriate next step after explaining the test results?
options: Let the coach overrule the clinical findings
Clear the athlete because denying selection is unfair
Repeat only the easiest hop test and ignore the others
Discuss risks, goals and staged options
explanation: Return-to-sport is a shared, context-sensitive decision that should integrate objective findings, athlete goals, sport demands and the judgement of the relevant team.
